content.text:
I've built the demo as a single self-contained file, `index.html`, with no dependencies. A headless Chromium screenshot shows everything rendering correctly. The screenshot was taken before my last small change (the POLYS counter); I syntax-checked that change but didn't re-run the screenshot. I haven't tested it interactively in a browser, so the buttons, slider and drag/zoom haven't been clicked.

**Renderer:** it projects the 3D scene onto the full-screen `<canvas id="c">` by hand. It hides faces turned away from the camera, cuts off geometry that's behind the camera, shades each face by a single light direction, and draws everything back to front so nearer objects cover farther ones.

**Scene:**
- **Structure:** six neon-edged boxes with 6 faces each, giving the 36 box faces. They are the two-tier platform, the twin pillars, the lintel and the crown cap.
- **Crystals:** six octahedra (8 triangles each, so 48) circle the portal while bobbing and spinning, each in its own colour.
- **Portal core:** a pulsing glow with swirling arms between the pillars. Two rings spin in opposite directions around it and pass correctly in front of and behind the other objects.
- **Floor:** a cyber grid in cyan and magenta that scrolls and fades out toward the edges, with a purple glow under the platform.
- **Stars and particles:** 180 stars on a distant sphere twinkle and shift as the camera moves. 110 glowing particles rise from the platform and respawn at the bottom.
- **Background:** a dark radial gradient behind everything.

**HUD:** a frosted-glass panel showing NEON PORTAL 3D with FPS, POLYS and PARTS counters. A bottom bar has Pause/Play, Orbit ON/OFF, Reset (camera, speed and time) and a 0–3× speed slider. I also added drag-to-orbit and mouse-wheel zoom.

**POLYS counter:** it shows the full scene count of 84 (36 + 48) to match your spec. The renderer only draws the faces facing the camera, about 42 per frame. If you'd rather show that number, the per-frame count is already calculated in the code as `polyCount`.

The FPS showed 0 in my screenshot only because of how the headless capture runs; I haven't seen it count in a normal browser.
